summary: @qlik/nebula-table-utils 2.6.9 ships a preinstall dropper that fetches Bun and executes an obfuscated payload
details: The package.json declares a preinstall hook `node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, extracts it to a temporary directory, marks it executable, and then invokes it via `execFileSync` against a sibling file `math_init.js` — a 727KB single-line JavaScript file obfuscated with a rotating string-array cipher (WV8StW/n7gIxM) and hex-mangled identifiers. setup.mjs itself is obfuscator.io-style hex-mangled. The package's declared purpose is a React table-utility library (lib/index.js); math_init.js and setup.mjs are top-level and unrelated to that library surface. The preinstall dropper executes automatically on `npm install` and runs an opaque, obfuscated payload under an alternate JavaScript runtime, evading Node-based inspection. Prior legitimate releases in the @qlik scope do not ship these files or declare a preinstall script, consistent with a compromised or impersonating publish that grafted an install-time loader onto an otherwise-normal library tree.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
